TRAFFIC ADVISORY: The Trans-Canada Highway is reduced to one lane of alternating traffic between La Manche Siding and the turn off to Upshall and Little Harbour East. 

Whitbourne RCMP and first responders are responding to a motor vehicle collision between a commercial tractor trailer unit and a passenger car.

Motorists are asked to exercise patience and caution, and obey all instructions from police and other responders.

Updates to follow.

#nltraffic

First Time Since WWII: Japanese Troops Fire on Foreign Territory

For the first time since World War II, Japan deployed combat troops to Philippine soil — about 1,400 personnel — as part of Balikatan 2026, the largest iteration of the US-Philippines exercise yet. 

Japanese Ground Self-Defense Force troops fired Type 88 anti-ship missiles from Ilocos Norte and sank the decommissioned BRP Quezon roughly 50–75 km offshore, Japan's first use of the system outside its own territory. 

The drill, joined by US, Philippine, and Australian forces, simulates repelling an amphibious assault in the South China Sea, and China has condemned it as "remilitarization" and "playing with fire." 

The exercise runs April 20–May 8 with ~17,000 troops from seven nations.

🚨 🇯🇵 🇵🇭 🇺🇸
Historic moment: Japanese troops fire on foreign territory for the first time since World War II

During the massive Balikatan 2026 military exercise, about 1,400 Japanese Ground Self-Defense Force troops deployed to the Philippines and fired Type 88 anti-ship missiles from Ilocos Norte. 

They successfully sank the decommissioned Philippine ship BRP Quezon, roughly 50–75 km offshore.

This marks the first combat use of the Japanese missile system outside Japan’s territory since WWII.

The drill involving the US, Philippines, Australia, and others (total 17,000 troops from 7 nations) simulates defending against an amphibious assault in the South China Sea. It runs from April 20 to May 8.

China has strongly condemned the exercise as “remilitarization” and “playing with fire.”

Source: Official military statements
